clue.text: Unconventional European community placed in the middle

parts.note: centric means central, located at the centre

explanation.surface: Something odd about a European body being positioned at the centre of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unconventional is odd or quirky in behaviour, a synonym.

clue.text: Linkman of comedy through Spain

parts.note: com is the clipped form of comedy, as in sitcom or romcom
per means by way of or through, as in 'per post'
E is the international vehicle registration code for Spain

explanation.surface: A presenter of comedy shows working through Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A linkman is the presenter who introduces acts on a show, a synonym of host.

clue.text: Select a former region

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a tract is an area or region of land

explanation.surface: Choosing an area that used to be a territory.
explanation.definitionFit: To select is to pick out or draw from a larger body, a verb synonym.

clue.text: An even numbered coin is worthless

explanation.surface: A coin bearing an even number turns out to have no value.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin worth two pence carries the even number two; as an adjective the word means cheap or of trifling value.

clue.text: Isn't able to start equine racing at this speed

parts.note: can't is the contraction meaning is not able

indicators.note: start asks for the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A horse that cannot get going in a race runs at a particular gait.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a horse's gait between trot and gallop, so a pace or speed.

clue.text: Justified conflict but stormed about afterwards

indicators.note: afterwards places the stormed-about word after the conflict word in the build

parts.note: war is armed conflict
to have stormed about something is to have ranted, raged loudly

explanation.surface: A fight was deemed justifiable, yet someone raged about it later.
explanation.definitionFit: Warranted means given proper grounds, a synonym of justified.

clue.text: Venture to quietly take possession again

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
to resume is to take back or reoccupy something, as in resuming one's seat

explanation.surface: Daring to reclaim something without making a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: To venture an opinion is to dare or take the liberty, which is to presume.

clue.text: Wild puma led it to the range

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of the following words run out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: An untamed big cat guided someone to the mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Amplitude is breadth, extent or scope, a synonym of range.

clue.text: A ragman files his letters in a different order

definitions.text: A ragman files his letters in a different order

indicators.note: the words say outright that these letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rag-and-bone man sorts his post into a new sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds and describes the answer: rearranging the letters of 'A ragman' produces a word for exactly such a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by rearranging the letters of another is this wordplay device.

clue.text: Feeling caused by drug movement

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
motion means movement

explanation.surface: A sensation brought on by a narcotic's effect on the body.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a feeling such as joy or anger, a synonym.

clue.text: By the sound of it, rushed the hill

indicators.note: these words tell the solver to go by how a word is pronounced

parts.note: tore means rushed or dashed

explanation.surface: Apparently someone dashed up the slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky hill or peak, especially on Dartmoor in south-west England.

clue.text: Begin searching other latitudes for the sun

indicators.note: Begin asks for the opening letter of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: Start looking in different parts of the world for sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sol is the Latin name for the sun, used in English for it too.

clue.text: Caged wild animals emerge in a terrible state

indicators.note: being in a terrible state means the letters are in disarray and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Animals kept behind bars come out looking awful.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept in captivity for show.

clue.text: A Latin fanatic follows one Roman citizen

indicators.note: follows places the rearranged letters after the numeral

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: fanatic suggests wild, frenzied behaviour, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An enthusiast for the old language pursues a single Roman.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of modern Rome is a national of Italy.

clue.text: Communicate beyond with German

parts.note: trans- is the prefix meaning across or beyond
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: Getting a message across to a German companion.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit is to pass on or send a message, a synonym of communicate.

clue.text: Tyneside town abandoned by "appleman"!

explanation.surface: A northern English town deserted by an apple seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned by' is a link here; Newton is a place near the Tyne in Northumberland, and Isaac Newton is the 'appleman' of the falling-apple story about gravity.
explanation.definitionFit: A village of this name lies by the Tyne; the physicist is linked with an apple that prompted his theory of gravity.

clue.text: Twit with no feeling up top!

parts.note: numb means without sensation
the skull is what sits up top, the head

explanation.surface: An idiot with nothing going on in the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A numbskull is a stupid person, a synonym of twit or fool.

clue.text: Military boss, volunteers, ambassador, duke and gunners are all more than two-faced!

parts.note: OC is officer commanding, a unit's military boss
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: A list of officers and dignitaries, all accused of being worse than hypocrites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-faced' suggests deceit, but the definition is literal: these solids have eight faces each, far more than two.
explanation.definitionFit: These solid shapes each have eight flat faces, so far more than two.

clue.text: Ride a bike around Ontario in bad weather

indicators.note: around means the cycling word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: to cycle is to ride a bicycle
ON is the postal abbreviation for the Canadian province of Ontario

explanation.surface: Pedalling round a Canadian province during a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclone is a violent rotating storm, an example of bad weather.

clue.text: Jewellery made from bottle top and string

parts.note: the neck is the top part of a bottle
a lace is a cord or string, as in a shoelace

explanation.surface: Making a bead piece from the top of a bottle and some thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklace is a piece of jewellery worn around the throat.

clue.text: Noticed last letter came first in publishing embargo

indicators.note: the final letter of the word noticed is moved to the front

explanation.surface: Someone spotted that the final character led the way in a ban on printing.
explanation.walkthrough: A D-notice is a British government request asking editors not to publish material harmful to national security.
explanation.definitionFit: This official notice asks the press not to print certain security matters, a kind of embargo.

clue.text: A half each of Edam, ibex and kale can be eaten

indicators.note: a half of each word is taken: the front halves of the cheese and the goat, the back half of the vegetable
and extends the half-each instruction to the final word, where its back half is taken

explanation.surface: Cheese, a mountain goat and a leafy green are all fit to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A half each of' governs all three foods: the front halves of the cheese and the goat, then, after 'and', the back half of the leafy vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible describes anything fit to be eaten as food.

clue.text: Although unlicensed, I will be here in France starting tomorrow

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
ici is French for here

indicators.note: starting asks for the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone without a permit promises to be in France from tomorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means not permitted by law, close to unlicensed.

clue.text: Having fibbed have to take a prone position

parts.note: lied means told a fib
to own is to have or possess

explanation.surface: After telling untruths, someone has to lie flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie down is to stretch out flat, horizontally on the ground.

clue.text: Cotton square, a group she follows

indicators.note: follows places the girl's name after the group word

parts.note: a band is a group, as of musicians
Anna is a girl's name, standing for any she

explanation.surface: A woman trails a band wearing a cotton scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandanna is a square of coloured cotton worn as a scarf or headband.

clue.text: Put an arm up to discern a lump

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gun is a firearm, an arm
to get something is to understand or discern it

explanation.surface: Raising a weapon to make out a lump.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a small lump, especially of gold.

clue.text: United nations were practised but not specially trained

parts.note: skilled means practised or expert

explanation.surface: The world body was experienced but lacked specialist training.
explanation.definitionFit: Unskilled describes workers lacking specialised training.

clue.text: Gear worn by knight with sex appeal!

parts.note: K is the chess notation for king, here used as the abbreviation for knight
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Equipment worn by an attractive knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit is a set of equipment or clothing, a synonym of gear.

clue.text: Work unit used by some energetic sportsmen

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A measure of effort favoured by lively athletes.
explanation.definitionFit: The erg is a small unit of work or energy in the centimetre-gram-second system.

clue.text: Lash cow performing a jump

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters put on a show and move into a new order

explanation.surface: Whipping a cow so it leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A salchow is a figure-skating jump taken off from one skate's back inside edge.

clue.text: Alfalfa found near Swiss lake

explanation.surface: A fodder crop is grown close to a lake in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is the British name for the fodder plant alfalfa; Lake Lucerne is in central Switzerland.

clue.text: Tear back in, then starts shouting menaces

indicators.note: in means the reversed word goes inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means the word tear is read in reverse

parts.note: the word tear, here intended to be reversed

indicators.note: starts asks for the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone rips something up and then starts yelling threats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' should turn the word tear around and 'in' puts it inside the then-plus-first-letter group; read strictly the reversal gives RAET, so the setter transposed two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Menaces as a verb means intimidates or puts in danger, the same as threatens.
